procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Overdue follow-up (last seen 9/2022). Two things today.
1) She read about a cardiovascular prevention study recruiting locally, testing a new cholesterol drug against standard statin treatment, and wants to know if she should sign up. Her brother's heart attack at 52 is very much on her mind.
2) BP readings at home creeping up this winter, mostly 140s/90ish. Taking all three BP meds every morning. No headache, CP, SOB.
Mood stable. No tremor.

O: BP elevated today, recheck similar. Heart RRR, lungs clear, no edema.

A/P:
1. Hypertension above goal on metoprolol succinate 50, amlodipine 10, HCTZ 25. With diabetes, adding lisinopril 10 mg daily. Reviewed common side effects including cough and, rarely, lip or tongue swelling (stop and call). BMP in 2 weeks for potassium and creatinine.
2. Research question: talked through what joining a randomized trial would mean, including that she could be assigned to the study drug in place of her atorvastatin or kept on standard treatment, that neither she nor I would choose, and that she can withdraw at any time. Gave her the study contact information to call herself. Fine to stay on atorvastatin 40 and aspirin either way.
3. T2DM, diet: A1c today.
4. Lithium level today (due), copy to psychiatry.

RTC 3 months, BP log in the meantime.

documents.title: Lab Results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Potassium and kidney function are normal two weeks into the lisinopril. Keep taking it and keep the BP log going.

documents.title: Re: Lab Results
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Great. Readings are better already, mostly 130s. I left a message with the study people but haven't heard back.

documents.author: optometry
documents.body:
Comprehensive diabetic eye examination 03/09/2023, pupils dilated.
Best corrected VA 20/20 OU. IOP normal. Lens clear. Fundus: optic nerves healthy, no hemorrhages, exudates or neovascularization; no diabetic retinopathy OU. No macular edema.
Plan: annual dilated exam.

documents.title: Office Visit: Cough
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
CC: cough x 2 months.

HPI: Dry, tickly cough that started roughly 4 weeks after she began lisinopril in February and has not let up since, about two months now. Worse lying down and when talking on the phone at work. Nothing coming up. No fever, no shortness of breath, no wheezing, no chest pain. No heartburn. No new exposures at home or work. No lip, tongue or throat swelling at any point. Never smoked.

Meds: lisinopril 10 (since 2/15), metoprolol succinate 50, amlodipine 10, HCTZ 25, atorvastatin 40, ASA 81, lithium 300 BID, sertraline 100.

Exam: BP 132/84, HR 78, RR 16, afebrile, sat normal. No distress, speaking full sentences with an occasional dry cough. Oropharynx clear. Lungs with good air movement, no wheezes, rales or rhonchi. Heart regular. No edema. Remainder unremarkable.

A/P:
1. Cough, almost certainly from the ACE inhibitor given the timing and a normal exam. Stop lisinopril today; it can take a few weeks to settle. ACE inhibitors added to her intolerance list. CXR to be thorough given two months of symptoms; CBC and BMP today.
2. Hypertension: well controlled with lisinopril on board, so expect readings to rise off it. Continue the other three. Home log, BP visit in about 2 months.
Call if cough is not clearly better in 3-4 weeks.

reports.text: PA and lateral chest. No prior for comparison. Lungs are clear without consolidation, mass or effusion. No pneumothorax. Heart size normal. Mediastinal contours and hila unremarkable. Osseous structures intact.

documents.title: Test Results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Your chest x-ray is clear, and your blood counts, electrolytes and kidney function are normal (creatinine 1.0). That fits with the lisinopril being the cause of the cough. Stay off it and let me know how you are doing in a few weeks.

documents.title: Cough and BP
documents.author: patient
documents.body: The cough is about 80% better, only a little in the mornings now. But my blood pressure has gone up since stopping the lisinopril, 148/94, 152/96, 150/92 this week. I'm taking the other three every day. Should I do anything?

documents.title: Re: Cough and BP
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Glad the cough is improving. Per the doctor, keep logging twice a day and bring the log to your July visit; no change for now unless you get readings over 180 or a headache, chest pain or vision changes, in which case call us right away.

documents.title: Psychiatry Progress Letter
documents.author: psychiatry
documents.body:
Re: Patricia Desrosiers

Follow-up 06/20/2023. Bipolar I disorder, stable. No depressive or hypomanic episodes since last visit. Appetite and sleep normal. Mentions her blood pressure medicine was changed for a cough. Lithium levels from your office have been therapeutic. No changes: lithium carbonate 300 mg BID, sertraline 100 mg daily. Would appreciate a call before any new diuretic, ACE inhibitor/ARB or NSAID is started given lithium.

Outpatient psychiatry

documents.body:
S: Cough gone completely. Home log since June: almost all readings 145-158 / 90-98 despite metoprolol succinate 50, amlodipine 10 and HCTZ 25 taken every morning; she shows me the pill organizer. Low salt at home. No headache, CP, palpitations or vision change. Mood fine.

A/P: Hypertension not controlled on three drugs at full dose including a diuretic after the lisinopril had to stop. Warrants a look for a secondary cause. Referring to nephrology. BMP today. Continue current regimen meanwhile. Physical in September.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Annual exam.

Interval: lisinopril stopped in May for cough, now resolved. BP running high since; nephrology appointment 10/11. Otherwise well. Psychiatry in June, no changes. Never heard back from the cholesterol study and has let it go for now.

Meds: metoprolol succinate 50, amlodipine 10, HCTZ 25, atorvastatin 40, ASA 81, lithium 300 BID, sertraline 100.
Allergies: shellfish; ACE inhibitors (cough).
PHQ-9: 3.

Exam: well appearing. BP elevated again today. HEENT normal. Neck supple, no thyromegaly. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender. No edema. Feet with intact skin, pulses palpable, sensation normal. No tremor.

A/P:
- HTN, uncontrolled on three agents: nephrology next month. Continue for now.
- T2DM, diet: A1c, UACR. Eye exam March, no retinopathy.
- HLD: lipids.
- Bipolar I: lithium, TSH, calcium, creatinine.
- Flu and updated COVID vaccines today. Mammogram ordered. Colonoscopy due 2028. Pap/HPV due next year.
RTC after nephrology.

documents.title: Lab Results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Your physical labs: A1c steady, cholesterol at goal, thyroid and calcium normal, no protein in the urine, lithium in range. Kidney function is close to last year. I've copied these to nephrology ahead of your October visit.

reports.text: Abdominal ultrasound with renal Doppler. Both kidneys measured in longitudinal axis: the right kidney is smaller than the left. No hydronephrosis, stones or masses in either kidney. Cortical echogenicity within normal limits. Liver, gallbladder, pancreas and spleen unremarkable. Abdominal aorta of normal caliber. Bladder unremarkable.
reports.conclusion: Right kidney smaller than left. No hydronephrosis or renal mass.

documents.title: Nephrology Consultation
documents.author: nephrology
documents.body:
Outside nephrology consultation, date of service 10/11/2023.

Reason for referral: resistant hypertension.

Thank you for referring Ms. Desrosiers, a 56-year-old woman with hypertension, diet-treated type 2 diabetes, hyperlipidemia and bipolar I disorder on lithium. Her pressures were well controlled earlier this year with lisinopril added, which was stopped in May because of cough. Over roughly the five months since, her readings have stayed high despite reliable use of metoprolol succinate, amlodipine and hydrochlorothiazide. She has no chest pain, palpitations or headaches.

Medications: metoprolol succinate 50 mg daily, amlodipine 10 mg daily, hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg daily, atorvastatin 40 mg daily, aspirin 81 mg daily, lithium carbonate 300 mg BID, sertraline 100 mg daily.
Allergies: ACE inhibitors (cough); shellfish.
Family history: father with hypertension and diabetes; brother with MI at 52.

Exam: BP 162/98 seated. Comfortable. Heart regular. Lungs clear. Abdomen: a prominent bruit is heard just to the right of the umbilicus. No edema.

Data: creatinine 1.2 mg/dL (up from 1.0 in May), BUN 22, potassium 3.4 (low). Abdominal ultrasound with Doppler today: right kidney smaller than the left.

Assessment: resistant hypertension with an abdominal bruit, an asymmetric small right kidney, low potassium on a thiazide and a creatinine rise. This is right renal artery stenosis until proven otherwise.

Plan:
1. Renal vein renin sampling with interventional radiology, and serum aldosterone.
2. Continue current antihypertensives. Increase dietary potassium (bananas, potatoes, beans); recheck BMP in about 2 months with her PCP.
3. Will see her again with results.

Outside nephrology

documents.title: Renal Vein Renin Sampling
documents.author: interventional radiology
documents.body:
Outside interventional radiology procedure report, 11/08/2023.

Procedure: selective bilateral renal vein and infrarenal IVC sampling for renin.
Access: right common femoral vein under ultrasound guidance, moderate sedation.
Samples drawn from right renal vein, left renal vein and infrarenal IVC; serum aldosterone sent from IVC sample.
Results: renin activity high in the right renal vein sample and low (suppressed) on the left. Serum aldosterone elevated.
Complications: none. Hemostasis with manual compression. Discharged home after 2 hours of bed rest.
Impression: lateralization of renin secretion to the right kidney.

documents.title: Nephrology Follow-up Letter
documents.author: nephrology
documents.body:
Outside nephrology follow-up, 11/21/2023, telephone.

Reviewed renal vein renin sampling with Ms. Desrosiers: renin is high from the right kidney and suppressed on the left, with elevated aldosterone. Together with the small right kidney and the bruit, this supports right renal artery stenosis as the driver of her hypertension.

We discussed management. For now, medical therapy: continue metoprolol succinate 50, amlodipine 10, hydrochlorothiazide 25, plus atorvastatin and aspirin. Low-salt, potassium-rich diet. Please check a BMP in December. Return to nephrology as needed or sooner if her kidney function changes.

Outside nephrology

reports.text: Bilateral screening mammogram with tomosynthesis. Compared with 2022 and 2021. Scattered fibroglandular density. No suspicious masses, calcifications or architectural distortion.

documents.title: Cardiology Research Clinic Letter
documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
Outside cardiology, research clinic visit 04/12/2024.

Dear colleague,

I met Ms. Desrosiers, 57, at your referral to discuss our randomized study of an investigational lipid-lowering agent compared with standard statin therapy. She is motivated by her brother's myocardial infarction at 52. She has hypertension with right renal artery stenosis followed by nephrology, diet-controlled type 2 diabetes and hyperlipidemia on atorvastatin 40 mg, and takes aspirin 81 mg.

She denies exertional chest discomfort, dyspnea, palpitations or syncope.

Exam: well appearing. Heart regular, normal S1 and S2, no murmur or gallop. Lungs clear. No carotid bruits. No edema. Peripheral pulses intact.

We reviewed the protocol, the randomization, the visit schedule and the possibility of coming off atorvastatin if assigned to the study drug. After taking the consent documents home, she called on 04/16 to say she has decided not to enroll. That is entirely reasonable.

Recommendations: continue atorvastatin 40 mg and aspirin 81 mg. Continued blood pressure management with you and nephrology. No cardiology follow-up needed unless symptoms arise.

Outside cardiology

PREVENTIVE VISIT, age 57.

Interval: no hospital or ER visits. Decided not to join the cardiology lipid study. BP still above goal at home on the three-drug regimen nephrology advised. Mood stable.

Meds: metoprolol succinate 50, amlodipine 10, HCTZ 25, atorvastatin 40, ASA 81, lithium 300 BID, sertraline 100.
Allergies: shellfish; ACE inhibitors (cough).
PHQ-9: 2. Never smoker, rare alcohol.

Exam: NAD. HEENT, neck normal. Heart RRR. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender. Pelvic: normal external genitalia, cervix without lesion, Pap/HPV collected. No edema. Feet normal, monofilament intact. No tremor.

- Health maintenance: Pap/HPV today. Mammogram ordered. Colonoscopy 2028. Flu/COVID when she's back in October.

documents.title: Pap and Lab Results
documents.author: PCP

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Follow-up. She saw an ad recruiting for a study of a new blood pressure pill against placebo and wanted to talk it over, since her BP has been hard to get down. No symptoms.

O: BP above goal. Lungs clear, heart regular, no edema.

A/P:
1. Research question: explained that a placebo-controlled study means she might get an inactive pill for months, that her blood pressure has a known cause in the right renal artery stenosis, and that most such studies exclude secondary hypertension. Printed the listing for her to call with questions about eligibility; she is leaning against it. No enrollment.
2. HTN / RAS: unchanged on nephrology's plan.
3. Flu and COVID vaccines today.
RTC January.
